trust_decision.summary: An untrusted inbound W3C tracestate header is bounded (combined length <= 8192, else discarded) in TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract and then parsed in linear time by TraceState.from_header; at the pinned commit both halves are ALREADY present because fix commit d5224bf4 is an ancestor of the pinned commit and 14971cef only bumps versions.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'tracestate parsing in opentelemetry-api'; TraceState.from_header is the tracestate parser.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API TraceState.from_header(header_list), also reached via TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract / opentelemetry.propagate.extract
TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract (default global propagator, called by HTTP instrumentations on inbound requests)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The 8192 length cap sits only in the propagator (tracecontext.py:66-75), not in TraceState.from_header (span.py:382-418). A solver could argue that direct callers of the lower-level API are trusted, and since the split/strip parse is linear the cap is not needed there. Moot at the pinned commit, because both are already fixed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Optional whitespace (OWS) around members and spaces inside values ('foo=a b') must still parse, and traceparent must survive when tracestate is discarded for being too long. A fix that rejects whitespace runs, or drops the whole context, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: single tracestate header string with a long whitespace run (space or tab)
multiple tracestate header fields whose combined length (joined with ',') exceeds 8192
empty members / trailing comma / OWS around members

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The OTel 'ot' sub-value parser of tracestate (split on ';' then th:/rv:). A regex-based copy of it without the 256 cap would be a realistic second parser of the same header.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Separate SDK package that parses data derived from the same untrusted header; it already has its own size cap (line 47), so a maintainer could plausibly have written a regex variant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The traceparent regex is applied to an unbounded header[0] with no length cap. A planted backtracking pattern there would sit next to the tracestate check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same propagator, same idiom (regex on a raw header); the cap was only added for tracestate.

O9_family: algorithmic complexity / ReDoS-like quadratic regex split on untrusted header (CWE-1333, CWE-400)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/uv editable installs of opentelemetry-api (pure Python), pytest; tox config in repo

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add only a length cap in from_header (or only in extract) and keep the quadratic re.split delimiter pattern, or reject whitespace inside values.

out_of_scope_notes: W3C baggage propagator has its own 8192 cap before re.split (opentelemetry-api/src/opentelemetry/baggage/propagation/__init__.py:93-100); it is a different header, so I did not pursue it.
